title: The 0.91 correlation trap in market data
text: Hi, I'm Aishwaryia from the Mikrooft team. This video walks through why a real statistical correlation in market data doesn't mean you found a tradable signal. Two variables moved together for eight straight years with a correlation of 0 91. A model flagged it as a signal. Nobody asked why. Method correlation measures whether two variables move together. It says nothing about whether one causes the other or whether both are being driven by something else entirely.

title: What correlation actually measures (and what it misses)
text: Where it fails with enough variables and enough time, you will always find some pair that correlates strongly by pure chance. This is a known measurable effect called spurious correlation. And it gets worse the more variables you test. The fix causation requires a real mechanism, a reason it would actually move B, plus a way to rule out a shared underlying driver.
